name: CreditAccess Grameen Ltd
about: CreditAccess Grameen Limited is registered as a non-deposit accepting NBFC - Microfinance Institution with the RBI. It is engaged in providing microfinance services to women who are enrolled as members and organized as Joint Liability Groups. It also uses its distribution channel to provide certain other financial products and services to the members. [1]

statements.text: Revenue compounded 19.7% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 42.8%.
Revenue growth accelerated from 8% to 26% YoY over the last 4 quarters.

cash.note: For lenders, operating cash flow mostly reflects loan-book growth; cash conversion isn't a meaningful test.

flags.text: Promoter holding down 2.5 pp in a year (66.4% → 63.8%)

ledger.quote: ROA of 5.2% to 5.8%
ledger.statement: Raised FY27 ROA guidance to 5.2-5.8% (from 4-4.8%)
ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
ledger.evidence: H1 FY27 ROA was 5.9%, already above the top of the raised 5.2-5.8% range (C1). H2 includes planned lending-rate cuts of 50 bps per quarter (G11).

ledger.quote: ROE of 21% to 24%
ledger.statement: Raised FY27 ROE guidance to 21-24% (from 16-20%)
ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
ledger.evidence: H1 FY27 ROE was 23.8%, inside the raised 21-24% range (C1).

ledger.quote: We retain our AUM growth guidance of 20% to 25%
ledger.statement: FY27 AUM growth of 20-25%
ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
ledger.evidence: AUM grew 19.5% YoY to INR30,946 crore, below the 20% floor, and only 2.1% QoQ in Q2 (C1). Management itself expects group-loan growth to return to guided levels only in H2 (G7).
ledger.actual_text: AUM +19.5% YoY, +2.1% QoQ at Q2 FY27

ledger.statement: FY27 credit cost guidance of 3-4%
ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
ledger.evidence: Management says credit cost is 'within the guided range' (C2). The inputs do not give the H1 credit cost figure.

ledger.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan

context.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
context.text: Thank you, Abhijit. A very good evening, everyone, and a very warm welcome to discuss our second quarter and first half of FY27 business performance. We reported our highest quarterly profit of INR 502 Crore in this quarter, having grown fivefold over the past 5 years. Current financial year marks a clear turnaround, recording INR 995 Crore PAT in the first half as against INR 778 Crore PAT during the previous financial year. Our H1 ROA stood at 5.9% and ROE stood at 23.8%. We are delivering record profitability while remaining amongst the most competitively priced lenders across our product segments. Our lending franchise today spans across Group Loans, Individual Business Loans, secured business loans, affordable housing loans and 2-wheeler finance, with growth, margins and asset quality all moving in the right direction. Our AUM grew 19.5% YoY and 2.1% QoQ to INR 30,946 Crore. Disbursements stood at INR 6,355 Crore, up 19.4% YoY and 4.1% QoQ, taking H1 disbursements to INR 12,461 Crore. We added 2.3 Lakh new borrowers, of which 35% were new-to-credit, taking our H1 additions to 4.9 Lakh customers. We also opened 60 new branches during the quarter, expanding our network to 2,326 branches across 460 districts. Digital collections rose to 26.3% versus 18.1% a year ago. When we began building our retail franchise, our thesis was very simple. The customers we've served for years would need more than a Group Loan as their economic profile improves and financing needs expand. That thesis continues to play out at scale with regulatory support in place. Of the ~45 Lakh borrower base, 15% or 6.8 Lakh borrowers belong to Retail Finance. context.text: Renish, our current NIMs are at highest levels. And as you know, the lending rate is guided by our pricing policy, which takes into account several factors, including your credit cost, including your cost of borrowing as well as opex. Only lever today is if credit costs increase, that is when we can retain this pricing. Now the credit cost since we are publishing within the guided range and being driven by the pricing policy, this will be range bound. We have earlier also indicated we will do a 50-bps cut this quarter and probably 50-bps in the next quarter. The marginal cost of borrowing increase is slightly because of the mix of borrowing that we've taken right now and not necessarily indicating a higher increase point of time. We do acknowledge that the repo rates have gone up, but it will be gradually passed and that will go through. If, for example, if the cost of borrowing goes up in next quarter, we have the right to reprice or not necessarily pass back the 50 bps that is planned for the next quarter also. I think it is something that we work on. But at this point of time, we need to pass this 50 bps to the customer given that the credit cost has held its ground.

context.speaker: Nilesh Dalvi
context.text: Renish, Nilesh here. So I'll add a couple of points. So firstly, on the borrowing cost, we do have borrowings from a wide range of lenders. So there are more than 80 lending institutions. And obviously, the borrowing rates will be within the range. That's where the blended rate what appears on the balance sheet is around 9%. So in second quarter, obviously, we did a couple of NCD transactions. We had a couple of longer tenure funds, which obviously will come at a slightly higher rate. But at the same time, what we have to also look at is the loans what we are replacing. So like even in third quarter, we will see the marginal borrowing cost will be higher because we have done a USD 175 million ECB in month of October, which will come at a higher rate. But it will also replace the USD 200 million ECB, which is going to expire in the same month. And the new ECB what we have taken is at a lower rate compared to the previous ECB which is getting replaced. Now when I look at my borrowing for next 6 months, the amount what we are going to draw down at a similar rate of the amount what we are going to repay. So that's where we are of a view that our borrowing cost will stay in this 9.2% to 9.3% range till March. While we do have certain repo-linked exposures, but around 30% of our borrowings are fixed. 40% are linked to MCLR and balance 30% are linked to the loans which are linked to repo, they reprice at different points in time. So it is not that it will immediately kind of add to the corporate borrowing and the MCLR-linked borrowings, typically, they react with much lag. And today, given the liquidity in the system, we have seen instances in a couple of banks that the MCLR has even come down. So from that perspective, as of now, we have visibility on the borrowing cost. And

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: A clear turnaround: record quarterly PAT of INR502 crore, and H1 PAT of INR995 crore against INR778 crore for all of FY26 (C1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Q2 PAT was up 298.4% YoY and margin was 35.2% against 11.2% a year ago. TTM PAT is INR1,587 crore, while the latest annual ROE was 11.0% and 3-year PAT CAGR is -2.0%, so this is a recovery from a deep trough, not new highs on a through-cycle basis.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: AUM growth guidance of 20-25% retained (G3, G21).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: AUM grew 19.5% YoY and 2.1% QoQ in Q2 (C1), and group loans are below guided growth until H2 (G7). The INR50,000 crore CY2028 target needs about 24% a year (G14).

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: FY27 guidance raised on NIM (12.8-13.2% to 14.4-14.7%), cost-to-income (33-35% to 29-30%), ROA and ROE (G22, G4, G23, G6, G25, G1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: The starting guides were already worse than Q4 FY26 actuals of 14.2% NIM and 30.4% cost-to-income (C4). The upgrade largely catches guidance up to numbers already reported rather than signalling new improvement.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Borrowing cost will stay at 9.2-9.3% to March while 50 bps lending-rate cuts are passed on each quarter (G9, G11).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Repo rates have risen, 30% of borrowings are repo-linked, the marginal cost of new NCDs and ECBs is higher (C2, C3), and the Q4 cut is conditional. Whether H2 NIM holds is too early to tell.

bull.point: Profit recovery is real in reported numbers: Q2 PAT of INR502 crore (+298.4% YoY), H1 ROA 5.9% and ROE 23.8%, and H1 PAT above the whole of FY26 (INR995 crore against INR778 crore).
Guidance has moved one way, up: credit cost from 4-4.5% to 3-4%, ROA from 4.0-4.8% to 5.2-5.8%, ROE from 16-20% to 21-24%, with the H1 ROA and ROE actuals at or above the new ranges.

Franchise expanding: disbursements up 19.4% YoY to INR6,355 crore, 2.3 lakh new borrowers (35% new-to-credit), 60 branches added, digital collections at 26.3% against 18.1%, and foreign borrowing up from 21% to 24.4% of borrowings.

bear.point: Growth is lagging guidance: AUM up 19.5% YoY and 2.1% QoQ against a 20-25% guide, with group loans below plan until H2. The INR50,000 crore CY2028 target needs about 24% a year.

Peak-margin risk: management guides 150 bps of lending-rate cuts over Q3 FY27 to Q1 FY28 just as repo-linked borrowing costs rise. Its own steady-state ROA target of 4.5-5% is 70-130 bps below the FY27 guide.
Cyclicality and leverage: debt/equity 2.82 on INR25,128 crore of borrowings. The last downturn took annual ROE to 11.0% and margin to 11.2% in Q2 FY26, and 3-year PAT CAGR is -2.0%.

questions: AUM grew 2.1% QoQ in Q2 and 19.5% YoY. What H2 disbursement number gets you to the 20% floor, and how much of that comes from group loans versus retail?

What were H1 annualised credit cost and the monthly PAR 15 accretion rate, compared with the 30-35 bps a month that underpinned the Q3 FY26 guide of 4-4.5%? Why narrow the guide to 3.5-4% if the trend is improving?
If all three 50 bps cuts go through by Q1 FY28 and repo-linked borrowing reprices up, what is the FY28 NIM, and is the 4.5-5% steady-state ROA your FY28 base case?
